definitions.explanation: A set point in time by which something must be completed or submitted.
The date after which something is no longer valid or usable, such as a product's shelf life or a document's validity.

examples.japanese: {提出|ていしゅつ}{期限|きげん}は{金曜日|きんようび}です。
{期限|きげん}までに{書類|しょるい}を{出|だ}してください。
examples.english: Please submit the documents by the deadline.

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{込|こ}みの{期限|きげん}が{過|す}ぎてしまったので、{来年|らいねん}まで{待|ま}つしかない。
examples.english: The application deadline has passed, so there is no choice but to wait until next year.

examples.japanese: この{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}は{期限|きげん}が{切|き}れている。
examples.english: This milk is past its expiration date.

examples.japanese: パスポートの{有効|ゆうこう}{期限|きげん}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.english: Please check the expiration date of your passport.

examples.japanese: {賞味|しょうみ}{期限|きげん}が{近|ちか}い{商品|しょうひん}は{割引|わりびき}されていることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Products nearing their best-before date are often discounted.

notes:
USAGE:
A versatile noun used in both administrative and everyday contexts. As a deadline (sense 1), it pairs with {提出|ていしゅつ} (submission), {申|もう}し{込|こ}み (application), and {支払|しはら}い (payment). As an expiration date (sense 2), it pairs with {賞味|しょうみ} (best-before), {消費|しょうひ} (use-by), and {有効|ゆうこう} (validity).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {期限|きげん}を{守|まも}る: to meet a deadline
- {期限|きげん}が{切|き}れる: to expire
- {期限|きげん}を{延長|えんちょう}する: to extend a deadline
- {有効|ゆうこう}{期限|きげん}: validity period, expiration date
- {賞味|しょうみ}{期限|きげん}: best-before date
- {提出|ていしゅつ}{期限|きげん}: submission deadline

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {締|し}め{切|き}り: deadline (more casual, used for work and projects)
- {納期|のうき}: delivery deadline (business term)
